author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Use a USB controller through Android OTG
summary: Validate OTG host mode, data capability, power stability, Android events, and one device-specific PS2 mapping before trusting a wired controller session.
heroAlt: E149 USB gamepad beside an Xbox 360 controller as a reference for a wired Android OTG input chain

sourceLabels.android-usb-host: Android USB host behavior and attached peripherals
sourceLabels.android-controller-events: Android button, axis, and device event guidance

blocks.text: Validate the OTG chain before mapping buttons
Prove that the phone enters USB host mode, the adapter carries data, the controller receives stable power, and Android exposes gamepad events.
A charge-only adapter or marginal hub can light the controller while carrying no usable input data.

items: Phone model supports USB host operation through the chosen port.
Adapter or hub is documented as data-capable rather than charge-only.
Controller tested on another host or known to be functional.

blocks.text: Prove each link from port to PS2 input

items: 1. Close the emulator and attach the OTG adapter without the controller.
2. Connect the controller and wait for Android device recognition or input response.
3. Test D-pad, face buttons, sticks, and triggers at the Android event layer.
4. Open EmuCoreX and create a profile named for the wired device and adapter.
5. Map Port 1 once, rejecting duplicate keyboard or mouse interfaces.
6. Play a demanding scene while watching for power-related disconnects.
7. Unplug at the adapter, reconnect, and verify the same profile returns.
8. If a hub is required, compare unpowered and properly powered operation without hot-swapping storage.

blocks.text: Android-level detection separates USB host, cable, and power faults from an emulator mapping that can only work after events reach the app.
Accept the complete wired input chain
Android detects one stable USB game controller and the emulator preserves its mapping across unplug and reconnect.

items: The controller is visible to Android before emulator mapping begins.
Axes return to neutral and buttons produce single transitions.
Sustained gameplay does not trigger USB disconnects.
Lights appear but no events: replace a charge-only cable or adapter.
The device cycles on and off: investigate available power and connector stability.
Android sees a keyboard only: select a documented gamepad mode on the controller.
USB storage fails when the pad connects: use a powered hub and retest devices separately.

blocks.text: Disconnect the OTG chain, restore the prior wireless or touchscreen profile, and remove only the failed USB-specific map.
USB host power is a phone-and-hub constraint
A controller that works from a PC port may exceed what one phone safely supplies, especially beside storage; use compliant hardware and do not infer data support from LEDs alone.
